title: Sky Courier: Storm Run

selected_top_5.reasoning: The game is an infinite survival run with automatic forward progression, increasing speed, procedural obstacle spawning, distance-based scoring, and restart-driven replay.

Although movement is continuous rather than hard-locked to lanes, the road framing, central stripe illusion, left-right evasion pattern, and downward oncoming hazards strongly resemble lane-runner play.

The game uses glowing sci-fi colors, bright arcade effects, luminous HUD styling, and a futuristic visual identity that partially aligns with neon-runner presentation, even if the setting is sky-storm themed instead of abstract neon tunnels.

The player experiences a forward-running avoidance loop in a suspended aerial space, but there is no gravity-flip or inversion mechanic. This is a weak structural match based mostly on airborne runner feel.

Rising speed is a meaningful part of difficulty and the session rewards surviving under increasing pace, but the game is more survival-oriented than route-optimization-focused, so the fit is secondary.

uncertainty_notes: The strongest classification is clearly Endless runner.
The game could also be described as an arcade dodge-and-collect survival game, but that exact label is not available in the provided category universe.
Lane runner game is a presentational and feel-based match more than a strict mechanical match because movement is analog across the width of the corridor.
No shooter, simulator, puzzle, or tycoon categories meaningfully fit the observed code.
